📋 PATCH NOTES

What's new and improved in IMS Fantasy.

❓ HOW IT ALL WORKS
🏁 The Basics

You run a fantasy team of 5 drivers — one per division (D0–D4) — plus a constructor, bought within your credit budget. Every real IMS round, your drivers earn the fantasy points they score in their division's race, and those points are your score for the round.

Your constructor earns its BOTT points from every driver racing for that team across all five divisions — so a strong constructor pick pays even when your drivers have a bad night.

⚡ Scoring — the fine print

Points land live. During a race weekend, results are imported division by division — your team's points tick up as each division comes in. The home page shows which divisions are already counted (the ✓ D0–D4 chips).

Off-division points don't score for your fantasy team — with one exception. If a driver races outside their own division as a general reserve outing, those points count for their constructor's BOTT total only, not your fantasy team. Their ELO still counts, though — the rating a driver gains or loses in a reserve outing carries into their global ELO, so a strong (or poor) reserve drive can still move their price up or down even though it earned you no points. The exception: if that reserve was standing in for a driver on your team who missed the race, they do score for you — see 🔄 Reserve drivers & tokens below.

Your team is snapshotted at lock. What you score with is the team you had when the round locked — transfers made afterwards count from the next round. The 📸 toggle on My Team lets you view last round's locked team and its points any time.

✅ Check-ins — is my driver racing?

See who's shown up. During a race weekend, drivers check in for their session. On My Team and the Market, a driver who's checked in for their own division's race gets a green ring around their photo and a green tick — so you can tell at a glance whether the drivers you own (or are eyeing) are actually racing.

Updates through the weekend. Check-in data refreshes automatically, so ticks appear as more drivers confirm. No tick just means they haven't checked in for their division yet — it isn't a guarantee they're out, but a checked-in driver is confirmed in.

Matching is by the driver's Discord account (falling back to their name), and only counts their own division's session — the race that actually scores for your fantasy team.

🚫 Race bans

Some drivers get banned. A driver serving a race ban is flagged on My Team and the Market with a red ring and cross over their photo, plus a 🚫 RACE BAN badge showing how many races are left on the ban.

Bans count down automatically. Each time a race is scored, one race comes off the ban. When it reaches zero the ban lifts on its own and the warning disappears — so a "🚫 RACE BAN · 2" means they're out for the next two rounds.

The badge is there to warn you before you pick or hold a banned driver. Weigh it up like any other risk when planning transfers.

👑 Captains

Your captain scores 2× points each round. Pick one on My Team before lock.

Things people miss: if you don't log in, your previous captain carries forward automatically — and if you've never picked one, the app auto-captains your best season scorer, so you're never without the bonus. Selling your captain removes their armband for the upcoming round, so pick a new one.

🃏 Chips

🚀 Triple Captain — one round only, your captain scores 3× instead of 2×.

🃏 Wildcard — unlimited free team changes for one round. Rebuild the whole squad without burning banked transfers.

😇 Guardian Angel — pick any extra driver (any division, even one you don't own) and their points are added to your total for that round — a sixth scorer.

Each chip is once per season. Choose your moment.

💰 Prices — how the market moves

Prices, dominance and ELO price moves all settle once per round — after the D4 results come in (the last division to be imported). Earlier divisions' points land live, but nobody's price or dominance moves until D4 closes the round. Four forces move what a driver costs:

1. Dominance — how crushing their performance was versus their own division, compared to their previous race. The price shift is $0.1M for every 5 points of dominance change: beat your last showing and your price climbs, fall off and it drops. Big swings in form move the most money.

2. ELO — every race nudges price by their rating change. Rises are tiered: drivers under $15M climb fastest at roughly $1M per 30 ELO, easing smoothly to $1M per 50 ELO near the $30M cap — bargains climb quick, superstars don't snowball. Falls always bite at the full $1M-per-30 rate at any price, so overpriced drivers correct fast. This includes ELO from reserve outings — a driver racing outside their own division still gains or loses global ELO there, and that still moves their price even though the outing scored no fantasy points.

3. Non-finish penalty 💥 — every DNF, DNS or DSQ costs price, and repeat offenders pay more: the season ladder runs -$0.5M for your first, another -$0.5M for the second, -$1M for the third, and -$2M for every one after that. Crash-happy (or steward-bothering) drivers become cheap for a reason. The count resets every season, so everyone starts each season with a clean slate — non-finishes have been counting since Texas, Round 1 of Season 7.

4. Demand 🔥 — when 3+ teams own a driver, buying them costs a bit extra on top (shown in purple in the market). It's a flat surcharge based purely on how popular they are, not a percentage of their price — so a cheap fan-favourite and an expensive one pay the same premium at the same ownership. It grows as more teams pile in (and a little faster once 4+ own them), and unlike the forces above it isn't permanent: it fades if owners sell up. Popular picks cost a touch more; contrarian picks stay clean.

Driver prices live between $5M and $30M; constructors can reach $35M. Constructors are priced against their own season average — beat it and they rise. Tap any driver or constructor for their full 📈 season price chart, including your own buys and sells marked on the timeline.

🔄 Transfers

You get 1 free transfer per round, banked up to 3. Team changes beyond your banked transfers aren't allowed — plan ahead or save your Wildcard.

Swaps settle at the net price difference: sell a $10M driver, sign a $12M one, and it costs $2M of budget. Downgrades put credits back in your pocket — profit from price rises is real money for future signings.

🔀 Promotions & demotions

When the league moves a driver up or down a division, the fantasy market reacts the moment the roster is synced:

If you own them — they're automatically removed from your team (they no longer fit that division's slot) and refunded, with a notification sent so you know it happened. Cheap drivers (under $10M) refund their exact price so you're made whole; pricier drivers refund 75% of their value. You're then free to re-sign them in their new division, or spend the refund elsewhere.

Their price carries over to the new division, but their ELO baseline resets to the new division's standard — so a promoted driver is suddenly measured against tougher company, and a demoted one against easier. Expect their price to move accordingly over the next rounds: promotions often become bargains-in-waiting or overpriced strugglers, and spotting which is half the game.

⚠ Note that pricier drivers refund 75% of their value — owning a $20M star through a division move gets you $15M back, a 25% haircut. So if rumours of a move are swirling, selling first can still be the smart play.

📣 Fan Zones

Pledge yourself to a constructor and your fantasy points count toward their Fan Zone (leaderboard → 📣 Fan Zones). You wear their badge and colours on the leaderboard.

New for Season 8 — zones score on averages. Each round, a zone scores the average points of its members that round, and its season total is those round averages added up. So it's about how well a zone's fans score, not how many fans it has — a small zone of sharp players can beat a huge one. Every member pulls the average up or down, so a bad week hurts your zone too.

The pledge is locked for the whole season — no switching, no leaving until the new season resets everyone. Only rounds from when you join count; no retroactive credit. Your profile shows your share of the zone's points and whether you're carrying the zone… or being carried.

🎖 Badges glossary

🏆 won their division at the last race  ·  P pole position  ·  ⏱ FL fastest lap  ·  🧹 SLAM pole + win + fastest lap in one weekend.

On the leaderboard: ★ a team's current captain · constructor logo chips show each player's Fan Zone · row colours are Fan Zone colours.

🔄 Reserve drivers & tokens

If a driver on your team doesn't race, a reserve can score for you. When one of your fantasy drivers misses their division's race, the driver who actually stood in for their seat that round (whoever raced that team's car in that division) scores the fantasy points in their place, for that race only. That stand-in can be a driver from another division, or a guest who isn't a regular on the grid — it just has to be whoever filled the seat.

You get 3 reserve tokens a season. Each time a reserve fills in for one of your drivers, it costs one token. Substitutions apply oldest race first. Once you're out of tokens, an absent driver is simply left as-is with no replacement. A reserve counts even if they scored 0 — they still took the seat, so it still uses a token.

The one person who can't be the reserve is the absent driver's own teammate — the other regular in that same team and division has their own seat, so they aren't a stand-in. Anyone else who drove the car is fair game.

You'll always know. When a reserve steps in, that driver's card on My Team glows teal with a 🔄 RESERVE IN ribbon and the reserve's face over the original — and the points shown (and counted in your total) are the reserve's. The 🔄 Reserve Drivers panel (below your constructor) shows your token count and every swap. If nobody filled the seat, your original driver just stays put.

The captain armband carries over too. If you captained a driver and a reserve steps in for them, the reserve scores with your captain multiplier — 2× (or 3× with Triple Captain). The bonus belongs to the slot you picked, so the stand-in inherits it.

🏆 Championships & your trophy cabinet

Division titles are awarded the moment they're mathematically won. On the Results standings, once a leader's points gap is bigger than everything their rivals could still score in the races left, they're crowned 👑 CHAMPION — and it shows up on IMS Live too.

Your own trophy cabinet (on My Team and your profile) fills up as you earn silverware, each trophy stamped with the season it was won:

🏁 Round wins — top the fantasy leaderboard for a race weekend (once results are final). 👑 Championships — finish 1st on the end-of-season leaderboard. 🥈🥉 Season podiums — finish top 3. ⭐ Fan Zone wins — be in the winning Fan Zone at season's end (the whole zone gets it, shown with the team's logo). 💎 Top value — end a season with the highest total team value.

📅 The weekend cycle

1. Race week opens — make transfers, set your captain, watch the countdown. 2. Teams lock at the deadline (your line-up is snapshotted). 3. The weekend goes 🔴 LIVE and points land across two race days: D0 & D1 are imported together on the first day, then D2, D3 & D4 together on the second — your team's points tick up as each batch comes in. 4. Once D4 lands and the round is complete, prices move and everything settles. 5. Once the previous round's verdicts are settled, editing reopens — you bank a fresh free transfer and the next countdown begins.

Miss a deadline? Your locked team races as-is, captain included — you always score.

⚠ One-time reset: recalculates every driver's price from their current ELO using the new division baselines (D0:1800, D1:1650, D2:1500, D3:1350, D4:1250). After this, only dominance moves prices — running this again later will overwrite any dominance-based changes since.

This gives every driver a sensible starting price based on their current ELO (the same calculation as before — $10M at baseline, $1M per 18 ELO points either side). From the NEXT race import onward, both dominance ($0.1M per 5 dominance points) and ELO change that race ($1M per 30 ELO points) will move price together, on top of this starting point.

🏁 Season-start pricing. For drivers who stayed in the same division, price is mostly last season's per-race average (75%) blended with ELO (25%). For drivers who moved up or down a division (e.g. Higosh D4→D0), price is ELO vs their new division baseline — last-season points don't follow them. Own-division dominance ($0.1M/pt) is added on top in both cases. Clears price history so this is the clean starting point.

🧹 Price cleanup: an earlier bug let dominance push some drivers' stored prices above the $${PRICE_CAP}M cap (the cap is now correctly applied going forward). This re-clamps any driver currently over/under the floor/cap back into range — doesn't touch anyone already within range.

🧹 Fix stale "what changed" display: an earlier bug meant any driver who had BOTH a dominance change and an ELO change in the same import only showed the dominance portion on Market (the actual stored price was correct — this is purely cosmetic). This recalculates lastPrice from the already-stored dominance/ELO changes, without touching price itself.

🎰 Betting Office — odds

How each driver's odds are built, in order:

  • Price weight % — the base rating. At 70: 70% comes from the driver's fantasy price vs the rest of their division, and 30% from their form in that division — average points there last season and this, with their last 3 races counting double (each point above the division average ≈ +25 rating). A driver who hasn't raced in that division yet is priced on price only. 100 = price only, 0 = form only.
  • Price scale — how much a $1M price gap matters (rating points per $1M). Higher = bigger gaps between cheap and expensive drivers' odds.
  • Form weight — bonus/penalty from results in that division this season + last: wins 35%, podiums 30%, points per race 35%, vs the division average. Their last 3 races count double, and drivers with few races get a reduced effect. 0 = off.
  • Circuit weight — bonus/penalty for how the driver usually finishes at this track vs everywhere else (all seasons, all divisions). Capped at ±1.5×. 0 = off.
  • Pole spread τ — pole odds are purely qualifying pace (average gap to the quickest, track by track, last 3 sessions ×2). τ sets how much a pace gap matters: every τ% slower than the quickest qualifier cuts the pace share by about 2/3. Smaller τ = the quickest qualifier is a shorter favourite; bigger τ = odds bunch up. Default 0.40%.
  • Bookie margin % — the house edge built into every price.

Checked-out drivers are removed and the division is re-priced without them; odds also move with other players' money (max ±30%). Type a number into any Override box below to set that market's odds by hand for this round (blank = auto).

⏱ Pole odds — qualifying pace

Pole odds come from qualifying lap times (column H) in the .db — last season and this season. Any lap more than 5 seconds slower than the fastest lap is ignored. Times are compared track by track against the other drivers now in the same division, so a driver who moved up is judged on their actual pace, not their old division's grid. Each driver's last 3 qualifying sessions count double. It rebuilds automatically after every round import; press this to rebuild by hand (needs the .db loaded).

🔮 What-if odds

See what odds a driver would get in a different division — e.g. Higosh in E3. Nothing changes for players; this is a preview only.

⚖️ Bet verdicts

Fix any bet that settled wrong (or settle one by hand). Changing a verdict adjusts that player's coins by the difference and sends them a pop-up explaining the change the next time they open the app.

🎮 Games — lock / unlock

A locked game still shows on the Games page so people can see it's coming, but nobody can play it until you unlock it. Admins can still play locked games to test them.

⚠ Reset games

Wipes every player's PaddockDle + Grid points, streaks, stats, H2H and duel records back to zero, and starts a brand-new daily driver and daily grid immediately.

🧭 Driver career lookup

Every team, division and role a driver has had, season by season, straight from the loaded .db (pre-season and academy rows shown separately). Needs the .db loaded (Add Points → 📂 Load Database).

📊 All-time driver stats

Every driver in the games pool with their all-time numbers (used by PaddockDle, the Grid and Higher or Lower). Edit any box and hit 💾 Save — edited values are highlighted in amber. Clear a box to go back to the calculated value.

🏁 Current Season

This drives which season is treated as "current" throughout the app — past-season tabs on driver profiles, BOTT standings, and results all key off this. Set it to match whichever season is actually live right now.

Used to work out how many races are left for the 🏆 championship clinch/champion logic. Set this to the full calendar length so a title can be awarded once it's mathematically decided.

Wipe the reserve-driver system and start it fresh from the next round: past absences won't use anyone's tokens, and everyone's back to a full set of reserve tokens going forward.

📊 Division Baseline ELOs

A driver priced at their division's baseline ELO sits at $10M, ±$1M per 18 ELO either side. NOTE: prices are stored values now — changing a baseline does NOT move prices by itself. It changes the anchor used the next time you run 🎬 Replay Season Pricing or the one-time ELO price reset.

🗓 Race Schedule

Set upcoming race lock times. The countdown timer will count down to the next scheduled race.

📋 Bulk add from calendar (paste the season)

Paste one race per line as date - Name, optionally with (Sprint). The lock is set automatically to 1 hour before D1 starts (Sat 12:30pm). Use a range like 10/11 Oct — the Saturday is used. Add the year if it isn't ${new Date().getFullYear()}. Lines with BREAK are skipped. Rounds auto-number from the starting number below (existing schedule is replaced).

🔴 Live Race Weekend

While live, the home page shows the race as in progress instead of the next race countdown. Normally stamps itself automatically at team lock — use this to force it on (e.g. if the schedule entry was deleted) or end it early. It also ends automatically when you unlock editing or import D4 results.

🏁 Pole Positions (manual)

Set each division's pole sitter for a race by driver name (must match roster name). Shows as a P badge on My Team and the Results page.

🔍 Pole Review (from quali)

Computed pole-sitters from qualifying lap times (fastest lap per division). Review against what's saved, then apply. Requires running import_poles.py first to stage the quali data.

Pick a race to see computed poles.

👑 Fix Missing Captains

Fills in captains for any team that has none set for a race — carrying forward their previous captain, or auto-assigning their best season scorer if they've never picked one. Never overwrites a captain a player chose themselves. Runs automatically on every import; use this to fix a race that's already been imported.

📸 Refresh Race Snapshot

Re-takes a race's team snapshots from CURRENT team selections — use when a race's snapshot missed late signings (e.g. wildcard transfers made after the race doc was created). ⚠ Only safe while teams haven't changed since that race — i.e. during or right after its round.

🧹 Fix Duplicate Race

When the same round got imported under two different names (e.g. "Spa Francorchamps" and "Spa"), you end up with two race docs. Pick the one to KEEP and the duplicate to DELETE. This removes the duplicate's race document only — it does not undo any price/ELO/DNF changes that import applied. ⚠ After deleting, re-run pricing if the duplicate double-counted (see note below).

💥 Rebuild DNF Records

Recomputes every driver's season non-finish count and DNF price penalties from the race documents that currently exist. Use this after deleting a duplicate race to clear phantom DNFs — real non-finishes are kept, stray ones (from the deleted import) are removed, and the price penalty is corrected (refunding any over-charge). Safe to run any time; it reconciles rather than double-applies.

🐞 Bug Reports
🗑 Purge Phantom Driver

For entries that aren't real drivers (bad rows, test entries, duplicates with no real counterpart). Strips their points, DNFs and team history from every race document — so constructor totals and standings correct themselves — then deletes the driver. Any fantasy team fielding them has the slot cleared. ⚠ Permanent. If they're a duplicate of a REAL driver, use Merge below instead so the points are kept.

🔄 Clear Moved Driver From Teams

When a driver changes division, they no longer fit their old slot in anyone's team. This finds every team holding them in a slot that doesn't match their current division, clears that slot, and refunds the owner (exact price under $10M, otherwise 75% of value) — then notifies players. Use it after a mid-season division move if the roster sync didn't already clean it up. Safe to re-run; teams already cleared are skipped.

✂️ Remove Driver From One Race

For a driver who didn't actually race in a specific round/division but appeared in the import (bad row in the source data). Removes only that one result — their points, status and team entry for that division — and recomputes the constructor total for that race. Everything else about the driver is untouched.

🧹 Void a Round's Fantasy Points

Zeroes every team's fantasy points for one round on the leaderboard — use when a round awarded points nobody actually earned. Driver and constructor results, DNFs and race history are left untouched, so the Results page still shows what happened. Reversible: toggle it back on any time.

🔀 Merge Duplicate Drivers

When one real driver was entered under two names (e.g. coldpalmer & HPjones), merge them. All of the duplicate's race results, points, DNFs, team history and fantasy-team ownership are reassigned to the driver you keep, then the duplicate is deleted. ⚠ Permanent — run a data backup first if you can. Prices/ELO aren't recombined; the kept driver's own price stands (re-import or replay if you need it recomputed).

Import created stray driver_reserve_… duplicates (e.g. lots of the same person, or a driver who fell off the market)? This scans every driver, groups them by name, and merges duplicates into one — preferring the real seated driver over auto-created reserves. Results, points and ownership are preserved. ⚠ Permanent.

Merge every copy of one name into a driver you choose. Pick the driver to keep in Keep this driver above (e.g. the D2 Red Bull Zloober), then press this. Every other driver with the same name — whatever division or reserve copy — is folded into it: current-season results, finishing positions, statuses, archived past-season results, fantasy teams, lock snapshots and bets. The copies are then deleted. ⚠ Permanent.

Points look doubled/tripled after a merge? Load the .db, pick the driver in Keep this driver, and press this. It rewrites that driver's points and finishing positions for every round (this season and archived seasons) straight from the database.

📊 Market Price-Change Display

Hides the ▲/▼ "up/down since last race" tags on every market row, driver blob, and driver/constructor profile. The biggest risers & fallers ticker stays visible either way. Use this after adjusting prices manually so players don't see swings that don't reflect race results.
